steps.prompt_exact: I want a saveable, openable Gym Mirror Progress Shot Consistency Studio for tablet and desktop that helps me make comparable gym progress photos with pose, angle, lighting, background cards, privacy crop checks, retake warnings, a session comparison score, and a copyable shoot receipt, without needing to upload images.

Good. Now let me think through this carefully before building, since it has a lot of distinct subsystems (pose/angle/lighting/background guides, privacy crop check, retake warnings, comparison scoring, receipt) and needs to work with zero image upload — meaning all "comparison" has to be self-reported/structural rather than actual pixel analysis. Let me plan the structure and a design direction matched to the gym/mirror-photo subject before writing code.

Design thinking: the subject is a gym mirror progress photo — phone propped or held, mirror reflection, gym lighting, often a locker room/garage gym background. The real artifact this resembles is a film photography contact sheet / loupe tool, or a tattoo/photo studio reference card — something with frame guides, a light meter, and a clipboard receipt. I'll lean into "shoot prep + continuity report" rather than "fitness app" — avoid generic dark-mode gym-bro red/black gradients. A frame-and-light-meter aesthetic: graph paper grid for alignment, a literal "loupe/viewfinder" crosshair motif, warm paper-and-steel palette (this is a consistency tool, like a darkroom continuity sheet, not a hype app).

Let me set up the build.

Create working directory
Create working directory

Let me lay out the full feature/data architecture before writing any code, since this has several interconnected subsystems that all need to persist together and reload cleanly.

Core concept: No image upload. So "comparable progress photos" and "comparison score" can't be pixel-diffing. Instead the tool works as a pre-shoot rig + post-shoot self-report, where:

Setup card — pose, angle, lighting, background presets get locked as a "Session Recipe" (the thing that makes future shots comparable).
Live framing aids — on-screen overlays (crosshair/rule-of-thirds/silhouette guide/level line) the user holds the tablet/phone up against while looking in the mirror — this is the actual on-screen tool, since there's no camera feed to overlay onto, it's a companion reference card held next to the mirror, plus a physical phone-mount alignment guide.
Privacy crop check — a checklist + crop-frame preview using a generic placeholder silhouette (not a real photo) so the user can mentally rehearse cropping before they shoot, plus a face/landmark/mirror-reflection-of-bystander checklist.
Retake warnings — a checklist of common consistency failures (different shorts, wet hair vs dry, post-meal bloat, phone tilted) that flags before they "lock in" a session as compared.
Session comparison score — since there's no pixel data, the score is a rigor/consistency score: how well this session's recipe matches the locked baseline recipe (same pose? same angle? same lighting? same background? same time-of-day bucket?) — a legitimate, honest "comparability score," not a fake body-composition score.
Shoot receipt — a copyable plain-text summary of the locked recipe + checklist results + comparability score, meant to be pasted into notes or sent to whatever app stores the actual photo.

This is honest about what it can and can't do — no body analysis, no fake AI vision, just rigor-of-process tooling. That's actually the most genuinely useful version of this for someone tracking macros/lifting on a PPL split.

Let me also think about privacy: this should explicitly never touch image data, store nothing about appearance, and the privacy crop section should be a coaching/checklist tool, not anything that processes real photos.

Now the data model:

Planning notes for data model and screen architecture before writing code
Planning notes for data model and screen architecture before writing code

Plan's solid. One more thing to settle before coding: the privacy crop check needs a way to "preview a crop" without any real photo. I'll use a generic abstract silhouette built from simple SVG shapes (not a real body, not anything that could read as a real or sexualized image — a faceless mannequin-outline, like a tailor's dress-form sketch) as the placeholder, with a draggable crop rectangle over it. That keeps it squarely a rehearsal tool, not actual image processing, and avoids any content-safety gray zone since it's a abstract geometric placeholder, not a depiction of a real or specific person.

steps.response_exact:
This is the bug. `populateTodaySelects` only sets up the outfit input and the checklist — there's no change handler that writes selected dropdown values back into `state.today.pose`, `.angle`, etc. Let me view the full function.Found it precisely. The `onchange` handler on each select does write `state.today[g]`, call `persist()`, and call `renderRetakeFlagSummary()` — but it never calls `updateSaveSessionAvailability()`. So the underlying `state.today` data is actually correct after selection, but the Save button's disabled state and hint text are never refreshed in response to the change — they only get computed once at initial load (`updateSaveSessionAvailability()` is called once, near `renderRefCard()`/`populateTodaySelects()`, on initial script load and on tab switches/import/reset), not on every select change. That's exactly why it appears "stuck" disabled even after picking all six values.

Same gap exists on the outfit text input — though outfit isn't part of `todaySetupIsComplete()`'s check, so that one doesn't affect this particular bug, but worth being consistent regardless since outfit changes don't refresh the hint text either (the hint mentions the recipe name, not outfit, so it's lower priority — I'll focus the fix on the actual reported bug first, then decide if outfit needs the same call for completeness).

Let me check `todaySetupIsComplete()` and `updateSaveSessionAvailability()` again for confirmation, then check the checklist handler too, since the retake-flag summary changing could also plausibly want a save-availability refresh (it doesn't currently affect availability, but worth checking I'm not missing another related path).Confirmed — `todaySetupIsComplete()` reads `state.today.pose/angle/lighting/background/distance/time`, all of which the `onchange` handler does correctly populate. The only missing piece is invoking `updateSaveSessionAvailability()` from inside that `onchange` handler so the button/hint actually re-evaluates after each selection. The fix is a single-line addition inside the closure.For consistency, the outfit input has the same gap — it doesn't refresh save-availability either. It's not part of `todaySetupIsComplete()`'s gate, but since `updateSaveSessionAvailability()` is cheap and idempotent, calling it here too prevents any future drift if outfit logic changes, and keeps every "today" field input behaving the same way.Now let's verify the fix logically resolves the bug, simulate the actual state transitions in Node (no DOM needed since this is pure data logic), and re-run the full compliance + syntax pass before re-delivering.That confirms the underlying gating logic was always correct — the bug was purely that nothing re-ran it after a change. With `updateSaveSessionAvailability()` now called on every select's `onchange`, the button correctly flips to enabled the moment the sixth field is filled, in any order. Now let's confirm `updateSaveSessionAvailability` is reachable from that scope (it's a hoisted function declared later in the file, same pattern as before) and re-run the full verification suite.Both handlers wired correctly, the previous scanner-token fix remains intact, and every compliance check still returns zero matches. Now re-check structural integrity (function exists, hoisting, syntax) since this was a closure-scope edit.Everything checks out — syntax valid, all DOM references resolve, all listener callbacks defined, delimiters balanced, and `updateSaveSessionAvailability` defined exactly once and now correctly invoked from both today-setup change paths. Copy to outputs and re-deliver.The data was always being written correctly into `state.today` on each selection — the gap was that nothing re-ran the button's enable check after a change, so it stayed stuck on whatever it evaluated to at initial load. Added `updateSaveSessionAvailability()` to the select `onchange` handler (and the outfit input, for consistency, even though outfit isn't part of the completeness gate). Button now flips to enabled the moment the sixth of pose/angle/lighting/background/distance/time gets a value, in any order.
